bank_name: South Bangla Agriculture & Commerce Bank PLC
period_note: SOLO/STANDALONE basis, unaudited. Balance sheet is the 31-March-2025 period-end snapshot (reported), compared against 31-December-2024 (audited). Income-statement items are for Q1 itself (01 Jan 2025 to 31 Mar 2025) -- for Q1 the cumulative and discrete-quarter figures are identical, same as CITYBANK's convention. PAT fell 43.6% YoY (Tk.194.09m in Q1-2024 to Tk.109.51m in Q1-2025, both directly reported comparative figures in this statement) -- i.e. the profitability decline that produced FY2025's near-breakeven result was ALREADY clearly visible in Q1, well before the Q4 audit/qualified-opinion event. Asset quality moved only modestly in Q1 itself: classified loans (Note 8.11, Solo) rose from Tk.14,335.08m (31-Dec-2024) to Tk.14,409.67m (31-Mar-2025), NPL ratio from 16.17% to 16.37% (+0.20pp) -- a small move compared to the +3.43pp jump to 19.80% seen by Q3-2025 (2025_Q3.json), implying most of the FY2025 NPL deterioration happened in Q2/Q3, not Q1 or Q4. Similarly the loans-and-advances-only provision shortfall (Note 8.10) was essentially FLAT in Q1 (Tk.6,556.94m at 31-Mar-2025 vs Tk.6,558.39m at 31-Dec-2024, a marginal Tk.1.45m improvement) before growing sharply to Tk.8,019.93m by Q3-2025 -- confirming the shortfall's growth, like the NPL ratio's, was concentrated in Q2/Q3 rather than Q1. Combined with 2025_Q3.json's finding that the P&L/profit impact was then concentrated in Q4, the fullest read of FY2025 across all four quarters is: Q1 already showed a sharp YoY profit decline with only mild asset-quality slippage; Q2-Q3 saw the bulk of the NPL/shortfall deterioration while cumulative profit nearly stalled (9-month cumulative PAT of only Tk.117.69m despite Q1 alone contributing Tk.109.51m, implying Q2+Q3 combined added only about Tk.8.2m); and Q4 alone swung to an implied net loss of roughly Tk.111.2m as the year-end audit recognised the qualified-opinion-level shortfall. This note also independently reproduces the same Bangladesh Bank forbearance letter found in 2025_Q3.json's Note 8.10 (letter ref. DBI-3/132/2025-660 dated 27 April 2025, and Department of Off-site Supervision letter DOS(CAMS)1157/41(dividend)/2025-3115 dated 22 May 2025, both allowing FY2024 financial statements to be finalized without adjusting for the disclosed shortfall), plus a Q1-2025-specific data point: 'The provision requirement as on March 31, 2025 stood Tk.1166.87 crore against which the Bank maintained provision of Tk.497.44 crore' (i.e. the same 11,582.10m/5,025.16m figures in this file's provision_required/provision_maintained). DATA-QUALITY FINDING: this filing's own Net Asset Value per share (NAV) comparative cell for 31-Dec-2024 reads 13.23, which is ARITHMETICALLY INCONSISTENT with this same report's own reported 31-Dec-2024 total_equity (11,045,530,488) and paid_up_capital (8,241,916,500, implying 824,191,650 shares at Tk.10 face value: 11,045,530,488/824,191,650=13.4009=13.40, not 13.23) -- and disagrees with BOTH the bank's own audited FY2024 annual report (2024_Q4.json: nav_per_share=13.40) AND the later 2025_Q3.json filing's own 31-Dec-2024 comparative (also 13.40). Per this dataset's standing rule (prefer the arithmetically-consistent figure when a contemporaneous one is impossible), the Q1 report's own 13.23 comparative cell is treated as an isolated computation error in that one report and is NOT used anywhere in this dataset; this file's own CURRENT-period NAV (13.51, for 31-Mar-2025) is unaffected and IS internally consistent (11,136,242,384/824,191,650=13.512=13.51) so it is used as reported. Capital adequacy (CRAR/RWA/Tier1/Tier2) disclosures are not part of this quarterly unaudited financial statement (annual-report-only in this dataset).
